## {{< fa clipboard-list title="a clipboard with a To Do list" >}} Pre-class Prep {#pre-class-prep} 

### A. (Optional) Create a free Observable account 

You'll be following along and adding your own code in this [Observable Notebook](https://observablehq.com/@allisonhorst/eds-240-data-viz-in-plot-2026){target="_blank"} to create interactive charts with the Plot library in JavaScript. You don't need an account to work in the notebook; editing a notebook while logged out puts you in "tinker mode" where you can test and see changes, but your changes won't be saved.

If you do want to keep your work from today's session, you can create a free account on Observable ([observablehq.com](https://observablehq.com/){target="_blank"}), then fork the notebook above to create your own stored copy. Allison will show you how to fork a notebook at the start of the session. You're welcome to work in either tinker mode (no account needed) or your own forked copy today, but if you want to take the forking route please create your Observable account before class since you'll jump quickly into the code.

### A. Prepare your final presentation 

We'll use our last lab section to give and receive feedback on final presentation plans. To prepare:

1. Review the requirements for your final presentation, which are detailed in [FPM #5](assignments/FPM5.qmd){target="_blank"}, and consider your responses to each of them

2. Prepare a Google slide deck (or other presentation format, though it must be easily shareable with Sam, so that she can have it open and ready on her computer on the day of final presentations) with your visualization(s). You're welcome to present just your final data viz deliverable (e.g. infographic) on it's own (i.e. without a slide deck), though you should still be prepared to talk through the [required points](assignments/FPM5.qmd){target="_blank"}

3. Practice your talk! You don't need to have a *perfectly* polished draft presentation, but the closer you get it to your ideal version, the better. You'll be practicing your talk in front of 1-2 of your peers during section.
